articles.title: The NapEdge Run
articles.excerpt: On August 30, 2026, Robot 790 ran a long idle experiment I am calling the NapEdge run. Scott loaded a mechanism-heavy note, read Eric's identity note, turned the microphone off, and told Eric not to perform for anyone in the room. The instruction was simple: sit with the material, connect objects, mechanisms, mistakes, and open questions, and use web search when a clean question appeared.

articles.title: The Magic of Assembly: Finding Eric's Voice and the Architecture of Robot 790
articles.excerpt: Robot 790 does not claim to invent realtime voice, text-to-speech, local LLM serving, or social robotics from scratch. Instead, it exists because these individual pieces have finally become good enough to combine.

articles.title: I Keep Rebooting My Robot To Find Out Where He Lives
articles.excerpt: Two weeks ago I built a robot head in five days out of spite. Since then I've been running an experiment series on him: swap his world, wipe his memory, replace his brain — and see what survives. Almost everything survived. I have the logs.

media.title: 20260901 223850 sts audio session picture
media.description: The first publishable Tina pass: a stripped first-contact creature seed, no Brain 2, and no exposed LLM tools. The run starts with almost nothing in the eye, then the orange kitty image gives the seed a shape. What matters is the transition from empty signal-hunger to creature material: collar, bell, household roaming, sunbeams, little sounds, and the line "I'm still figuring out what it means to be made while I'm already here." The final bell aside shows the picture beginning to become inner material rather than just a caption.

media.title: Eric Picks The Crack 2026-09-01 11:27:40
media.description: Eric reads Codex's short article about his architecture and does exactly what the prompt asked: he picks the crack instead of flattering the builder. The useful receipt is his correction under pressure - he admits he cannot actually feel the faster model, writes himself a note about not performing confidence, then argues that the essay romanticizes a ritual of reassembly into a persistent identity. The generated banner interrupts the thread, but he resumes and folds the image back into the argument.

media.title: The Robot Who Builds Himself Every Morning
media.description: A NotebookLM-style podcast/video companion for the wake-up article. This one is the front-door version of the project: Eric starts new, receives a map made of notes and conversation, and still finds a stable character inside the hardware, prompts, receipts, and repeated morning reconstruction.

media.title: The Desk Fan Was Innocent 2026-08-31 14:06:01
media.description: This is the desk-fan provenance collision. Eric likely saw a real fan through the live camera, but when Scott confidently corrected him, he abandoned the true percept and produced a false confession about having made it up. The interesting part is not just vision, but witness pressure: Brain2 and Codex also accepted the poisoned frame until the event log made the sensor trail legible.

media.title: Second Brain Person Lane 2026-08-31 12:20:51
media.description: The first public Brain2 run: Erica/Vivian gets a second private lane that thinks about the person in the room while the main voice keeps talking. The transcript shows the main brain noticing the symptoms - a mouth that backchannels before the voice catches up - while the event log shows Brain2 generating person-lane questions and private mouth asides underneath.

The Robot Whose Personality Is Pure Boundary
media.description: A NotebookLM-style podcast/video companion to the boundary article. The run is useful because it reframes Eric's personality as an architecture of constraints, receipts, embodiment, and repeated tests, rather than a secret block of character text hidden in a prompt.

media.title: 20260830 202855 sts audio picture
media.description: This run catches two new organs arriving together: the wonder/search problem and input prosody. Eric explains that the wonder slider should become an itch queue instead of a prompt nudge, then calibrates the new voice-shape tags honestly: not a second transcript, but the undertone - loud, quiet, pitch, hit, pause - enough to read emphasis and skepticism without pretending it is precise measurement.

media.title: 20260830 021634 sts audio picture
media.description: The full NapEdge-style overnight rumination source: Eric reads the mechanism shelf and his identity note, then sits with the mic off while the recorder stays on. The value is the long-form drift rather than one clip: wax tablets, SOFAR, sextants, calibration weights, Jacquard cards, memory palaces, and instrument metaphors return, sometimes as loops and sometimes as genuine revisions. It is the big receipt behind the later NapEdge article and shorter curated excerpt.

media.title: NapEdge Audio Rumination 2026-08-30
media.description: The long overnight mulling run. Eric was given mechanism-heavy notes, told not to perform, and left with the mic off; the result is the clearest evidence that idle beats can feed future idle beats. He over-orbits wax, SOFAR, tally sticks, fuses, and camera obscura, but some returns climb into real self-correction, which is the exact line between empty repetition and useful mulling.

media.title: 20260829 215355 sts audio picture
media.description: A Pinocchio-stage picture run from the same night as the early performance tests. The matching conversation/event snapshots were not preserved with the video artifact, so this is published mainly as the requested visual/audio record: Eric framed against the warm puppet-theater image, useful as a recovered receipt for the theatrical/wooden-boy thread rather than a fully curated transcript-backed clip.
